text:
anna: Heads up — canary for r3456 shows a decode-path latency regression on short seq traffic, p95 ~2.8x vs baseline. Spikes started after the compile cache changes.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy r3456 -> sha abcdef completed (region: us-west2) :rocket:

kevin: Damn. I saw CI perf noise on the post-merge run but assumed transient. Which test / metric?

anna: Observed from per-route dashboards: shortseq-chat (<=64 tokens) p95 from ~30ms -> 85ms on the canary hosts. Throughput steady, CPU usage up.

sam: Any flamegraphs or profiler dumps?

anna: I pulled a perf sample from a repro run on a canary box. Key diff points: more time in kernel selection + a 3x increase in kernel compile time for fused-attn when compile cache miss happens.

anna: profiler snippet:
```
# short trace (aggregated)
30%  runtime::kernel_selector
22%  runtime::jit::compile_fused_attn
12%  runtime::kv_cache::lookup
8%   cublasGemmWmma
5%   memcopy
...
```

maria: compile_fused_attn? The change in r3456 invalidated the device-specific cache key (we switched the kernel fingerprint to include the fused-op DAG). If cache keys differ, JIT hits drop and we recompile at runtime.

kevin: Right — r3456 added DAG hashing to avoid subtle correctness mismatch across quantization modes. It fixed a correctness bug but probably changed the cache seed. We thought it would be safe because we prewarm on start, but canary nodes show dynamic compile during traffic.

sam: Could explain p95 regressions for short requests: warmup time per kernel matters more when seq lengths are short (lots of small calls). Long sequences amortize compile work.

ci-bot: 1 failing perf test: perf/regression/shortseq_p95 (post-merge) — delta +2500ms. See https://ci.example/redwood/3456/perf-run

anna: Action items I propose: 1) temporary revert of the DAG hash change 2) bisect to confirm it's the cache key variant 3) add prewarm in init path for fused-attn variants 4) add cache key migration script so we can avoid runtime recompile on rollout.

kevin: I can cut a small revert PR for the key change (r3456 revert) and push as hotfix to canary. If that drops p95 back we ship revert across clusters. Sam, can you run a comp-scan/bisect to ensure no other change caused this?

sam: On it. Running bisect across commits (r3440..r3460) now. Will instrument compile cache hit rate.

sam: Quick update — compile cache miss rate on fused-attn jumps from ~1% -> 65% on canary after r3456. Other kernels unchanged.

maria: Confirmed: fingerprint seeds include DAG hash string. The change appended the quant-mode name to the key. Our prewarm path uses model+device but not quant-mode, so mismatch at runtime for some routes.

kevin: Ok that pins it. Let's do revert + better prewarm. Revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3498 (wip).

anna: If we revert, we should still include a test to assert compile cache equivalence across our expected rollout permutations. Also add a CI perf guard for shortseq p95 so future changes fail fast.

sam: Note: reverting without prewarm might still hit recompile if some hosts already used new fingerprints in local cache. We'll need to drain canary and re-deploy cold with prewarm, or run a cluster-wide migrate to populate old-key artifacts.

kevin: For immediate triage: I'll cut the revert PR and trigger canary redeploy. Maria, can you add an init prewarm that touches fused-attn variants for common quant modes? Keep it low-cost.

maria: Will do. Prewarm plan: on startup, launch async compile for top 3 kernel shapes used by shortseq traffic; record metrics. We'll gate with env var ENABLE_PREWARM=true.

deploy-bot: Started deploy revert/pr-3498 to canary (region: us-west2)

ci-bot: Perf guard triggered on canary post-deploy: shortseq_p95 still +20ms but improved vs +55ms; compile-cache miss rate dropped to 4%. Full rollout on hold until 24h observation passes.

anna: Great progress. Let's keep the rollout blocked until 24h stable. Sam, please finish the bisect log and attach repro commands to the PR. Kevin, link the CI perf guard to the PR so it blocks merges until we add stronger tests.

kevin: Will do. Thanks everyone.

sam: Bisect results and repro steps attached to PR comment. Repro command:
```bash
./tools/run_perf_repro --model chat-short --seq 32 --concurrency 8 --measure p95 --region us-west2
```

anna: Filing postmortem notes and follow-ups in eng-runtime: create ticket to add cache-key migration helper and CI perf test.

maria: I'll follow up with a small RFC for cache-key stable migration patterns so we don't repeat this.

kevin: Closing loop — revert merged to canary, holding rollout. We'll reconvene if anything else surfaces. :thumbsup:
